package_info.why_malicious: The SolarWinds Orion platform was compromised via a supply chain attack in which attackers injected malicious code into the legitimate software update process. This code created a backdoor (SUNBURST/Solorigate) that allowed remote access and control of systems running the affected versions, impacting thousands of downstream customers including critical US government agencies.

execution_context.file_location: SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll (trojanized DLL within Orion update package)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: The code checks for signs of a legitimate environment, delays execution to evade detection, then establishes a connection to a remote command-and-control (C2) server to receive further instructions and exfiltrate data.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code is not part of the legitimate Orion business logic and implements stealthy network communication with external servers, which is not expected in a network management product.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal Orion DLLs should not contain logic to contact external C2 servers, delay execution for evasion, or await remote commands.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate software may check for updates or telemetry, but not with stealth, randomized delays, or awaiting arbitrary remote commands.
key_indicators: Network beacons to external, non-SolarWinds domains

attack_chain.action: Attacker injects malicious code into the SolarWinds Orion build process, trojanizing a core DLL.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is included in official Orion software updates.

attack_chain.action: Customers install the compromised Orion update, loading the trojanized DLL into their environment.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code executes on customer systems.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code performs environment checks, delays execution, and then initiates stealthy network communication with attacker-controlled C2 servers.
attack_chain.leads_to: Establishes persistent backdoor access for attackers.

attack_chain.action: Attackers issue commands via the C2 channel, enabling lateral movement, data exfiltration, or further payload delivery.
attack_chain.leads_to: Full compromise of affected networks and systems.

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected outbound network connections from Orion servers to external domains
DLLs with obfuscated or suspicious code in Orion installation directories
Processes loading SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll exhibiting C2-like behavior
file_indicators: SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll (with hash matching known trojanized versions)
Presence of unknown or modified DLLs in Orion application folders
network_indicators: Connections to avsvmcloud.com and related C2 infrastructure
Unusual DNS queries or HTTP/S traffic from Orion servers to non-SolarWinds domains
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor Orion servers for unexpected outbound network connections, especially to known C2 domains (e.g., avsvmcloud.com). Check file hashes of core Orion DLLs against known-good versions. Look for randomized delays in process activity and the presence of obfuscated or suspicious code within Orion DLLs. Use EDR or network monitoring to flag C2-like behaviors and lateral movement originating from Orion hosts.
